channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: The high street you knew has gone forever
item.description: The changing high street tells a wider story about regulation, cost and unintended consequences. When legal businesses are squeezed while illicit trade expands, communities do not become healthier or safer — they lose accountable retailers and gain harder-to-control markets. Tobacco and nicotine policy should pay attention to that pattern. If regulation makes responsible shops disappear, the gap will not stay empty for long. (Published on August 11, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Finding Optimism in the Tobacco Harm Reduction Maelstrom
item.description: Optimism in tobacco harm reduction does not come from pretending the work is easy. It comes from the evidence that change is already possible: smoking can fall, safer alternatives can reach people, and public health can move beyond abstinence-only thinking. The setbacks are real, from prohibition to misinformation, but so are the lives improved when smokers find a route away from combustion. Harm reduction is ultimately a reason to keep going. (Published on August 11, 2026byfiltermag.org)

item.title: US tobacco experts shift stance to back vaping as quit-smoking option
item.description: A shift among tobacco experts matters because it changes what smokers hear from the people shaping the debate. Backing vaping as a quit-smoking option does not mean ignoring risk; it means recognising that continued smoking carries far greater harm. For adults who have not stopped through conventional routes, e-cigarettes may offer a practical way out of combustion. Public health advice should reflect that evidence clearly, without stigma making useful options harder to discuss. (Published on August 12, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: Media Watch: Huffington Post on Nicotine Pouches
item.description: Media coverage can shape public understanding before evidence has a chance to. When nicotine pouches are framed mainly through alarm, important distinctions are often lost: they are smoke-free, they do not involve combustion, and they should not be assessed as if they were cigarettes. Scrutiny is necessary, especially around youth access and product standards, but reporting should not turn uncertainty into panic. Public health is better served by context than by headlines that make every nicotine product sound the same. (Published on August 12, 2026bydaily-pouch.com)

item.title: Ireland’s nicotine flavour ban ‘would trap smokers with cigarettes’
item.description: Ireland’s vape ban debate is becoming a test of whether public health can separate protection from overreach. Restrictions aimed at reducing youth use may sound straightforward, but they can also remove products that help adults stay away from cigarettes. The risk is a policy that looks tough while making smoking harder to escape. A better approach would target underage access and illicit sales without closing legal routes to lower-risk alternatives. (Published on August 12, 2026bysmokefreesweden.org)
